title: The Fake Surname Lists: How Memes Invent Genealogies
hero_object: 1808 Napoleonic Surname Registry & Linguistic Etymology Lexicon
hook: A meme gave you a list of surnames. Historical genealogy gives you something else.
punchline: A viral graphic is not a family tree.
visual_paradigm: Genealogical Archives & Civil Ledger Registry (Warm Parchment #FFFBEB, Sepia Ink #451A03, Archival Cyan #0284C7)

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: A meme gave you a list of surnames. Historical genealogy gives you something else.
scenes.on_screen: VIRAL SURNAME LISTS VS. REAL GENEALOGY

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: You’ve seen posts circulating lists claiming that any name ending in '-man', '-stein', or geographic names like 'Frank' proves someone is secretly Jewish.
scenes.on_screen: THE CLAIM: SPECIFIC SUFFIXES = SECRET IDENTITY

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Here is the linguistic reality. Names like 'Hoffman', 'Schneider', or 'Berg' are standard German occupational and geographic words shared by millions of Christians and Jews alike.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Before the nineteenth century, most European Jews did not use fixed hereditary surnames at all. They were mandated by secular laws like Napoleon’s decree of eighteen-oh-eight.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Families adopted whatever common regional names were assigned by local civil clerks. A name tells you about regional language, not religious affiliation.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Classifying strangers by surname patterns is bad linguistics and lazy profiling. Real ancestry requires authentic archives, not a cropped graphic.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: A viral graphic is not a family tree.
scenes.on_screen: A VIRAL GRAPHIC IS NOT A FAMILY TREE
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
